residual: P2: Three doc surfaces added by this slice claim that "a non-integer value" is discarded and announced as a `decision` event, but `agentCap` coerces with `Number(...)`, so a JSON string or one-element array that reads as a whole number above the default is APPLIED: it raises the cap and emits `agent-cap-override` with no discard announcement. Verified by execution against the real callable through slice_wave_harness.mjs at the shipped head 97fd3c3: `{s1: "14"}` -> title "agent cap reached (14)", agents_used 14, events `["agent-cap-override|{tier:1,default_cap:10,effective_cap:14}", ...]`, zero discard events; identical results for `{s1: [14]}` and `{s1: " 14 "}`, while `{s1: true}` and `{s1: 10.5}` do produce the discard decision event. The workflow's own comment on `agentCap` is accurate ("a missing, non-numeric or fractional value leaves the tier default in force"); only the three doc sentences over-reach, which is the defect class this run exists to eliminate. Not user-facing harm (the raise is what the human authorised and it is still recorded by its own event), hence P2 rather than P1.

P2: The run's binding shared constraint states new comments and new string literals must contain "none of `&&`, `||`, `?`", and slice s10's own Task 4 verification step requires that every hit of the same grep be executable code, "never a string literal or comment." Several newly-introduced string literals in this diff are natural-language question text ending in a literal `?` (the widened lost-slice question in the workflow, its test-file `LOST_QUESTION` constant, and the matching Python contract-test string), which is a literal violation of that constraint's wording. In practice the frozen gate (re-run at HEAD) reports no new function-level violation from this — its sole failure is the pre-existing, accepted `class_lines` debt on this same file (939 vs threshold 300, 812 at run base) — so the risk is disclosed margin, not an active breakage, but the constraint as literally stated was not honored and the task's own self-check grep (which I re-ran) turns up exactly these string-literal hits.

P3: `fullPipeline`'s agent mock is genuinely id-agnostic (it derives the dispatch role by slicing the label at the first colon, so it would work for any slice id containing no colon), but the paired `PIPELINE_LABELS` export hardcodes the `"s1:"` prefix onto every role key. The two exports read as a matched pair (one drives the mock, the other is the expected label set), yet only one of them is actually generic. This currently causes no bug because the sole consumer always drives `sliceFixture("s1", 2)`, but the generic-sounding export name invites a future test to pass a different slice id and get a silently-wrong expected-label comparison.

deferred: The signal is a slice-start snapshot, so one discard shape stays silent: an override that IS applied at slice start (event emitted) but is rendered unusable moments later by `maybePromoteTier` raising the review tier above it — for example `{s1: 20}` on a tier-2 slice promoted to tier 3, where `agentCap` then returns the tier-3 default 32 and the recorded `effective_cap: 20` never binds. The existing comment on `recordCapOverride` already caveats the snapshot, and Task 6's wording says "at slice start", so nothing written here is false; the goal of "a controller always learns the lever did nothing" is simply not met on that path. Worth logging rather than widening this diff for.

Every `decision` event feeds run_metrics: `decisions_total`, `autonomy_ratio` (`_autonomy_ratio` at run_metrics.py, "share of judgement calls the loop resolved itself rather than handing to the human") and `reversibility_mix`. A purely diagnostic discard announcement therefore nudges reported autonomy UP in precisely the runs where a human had to authorise a cap raise. The magnitude is one event per unusable override and the payload shape matches the existing tier-promotion decision event, so this changes no contract; it is a small metric-truth wrinkle to record, not to fix inside a narrow round-2 diff.
